roles.key_details: Publishes long-term pk_B=(rho,b), retains sk_B=s_B, and derives from the one-pass public value M1.
Uses pk_B, samples fresh short r and dither seed mu, publishes M1=(mu,u,h), and derives K_A locally; NGCC harness initiator keys are compatibility objects unused by the mathematical protocol.

forward_secrecy.conditions: Compromise of the responder's static secret s_B permits recomputation of past keys from recorded M1; no forward-secrecy claim is made.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: None in the standalone one-pass interface.
protocol_characteristics.transcript_binding: K_A and K_B are derived as KDF(nu, pk_B, M1) using a fixed 16-byte domain separator and SHAKE256.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Responder-static, initiator-ephemeral one-pass NIKE using public dithered split quantization and NewHope-style D4 reconciliation; the online message is a reconciliation transcript, not a ciphertext.

underlying_primitives.name: RLWQ-Z split quantization

components.name: mu

components.name: h
components.semantics: Packed public D4 reconciliation helper vector.

protocol_flow.semantics: Using pre-distributed pk_B, the contributor samples ephemeral r, computes the close product and K_A, and publishes M1=(mu,u,h); the public-key owner reconstructs its close product and derives K_B.

static_contributions: Responder/public-key-owner secret polynomial s_B and public key pk_B=(rho,b) determine the responder-side close ring product.
ephemeral_contributions: Initiator/contributor short polynomial r and dither seed mu determine u, local v, helper h, and raw string nu_A.
key_schedule.transcript_hash: The KDF input includes the complete public transcript T=(pk_B,M1)=((rho,b),(mu,u,h)).
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: K_A = KDF(nu_A, pk_B, M1); K_B = KDF(nu_B, pk_B, M1), instantiated as SHAKE256 over a fixed 16-byte domain separator, raw reconciliation string, responder public key, and complete one-pass message.
key_schedule.domain_separation: Fixed 16-byte KDF domain separator; separate labels for SHAKE128 public expansion and response dithers.
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: The specification directs implementations to clear ephemeral secrets and raw reconciliation strings after key derivation; the initiator API retains only the precomputed final shared secret in state.

correctness.relationship: There is one D4 reconciliation/key-acceptance event per published M1, so the protocol disagreement event is exactly rho_key = Pr[Rec(w,h) != Rec(v_hat,h)].
correctness.basis: Algorithm specification Definition 6.2 and Appendix C.1, especially Table 11. The submission warns that the double-precision estimator truncates below 10^-13 and the reported exponents are not certified cryptographic upper bounds; 5,000/5,000 test agreements per profile had zero observed failures.

security_claims.claim: Passive real-or-random session-key security is reduced directly to two decisional split-RLWQ advantages, reconciliation leakage epsilon_rec, key-rejection rho_key, and transcript-bound SHAKE256.
No authentication is provided by the standalone NIKE interface.
Active attacks, replay protection, identity/channel binding, UKS/KCI resistance, and decapsulation-oracle security are outside the submitted security experiment.

claimed_advantages.claim: Power-of-two public dithered quantization provides compact p-packed public keys and one-pass response messages.
Power-of-two arithmetic uses masking reduction and avoids prime-field roots of unity; one protocol syntax covers all five profiles.
Input-independent quantization error yields an explicit agreement-error expression and direct split-RLWQ proof route.
Portable C and x86-64 AVX2 tracks share byte-identical layouts and KAT behavior, with measured AVX2 speedups across all profiles.
Five profiles from 128 through 512 classical-bit targets share a unified code base and API flow.

limitations_and_constraints.description: The standalone construction is unauthenticated; replay, identity binding, channel binding, UKS/KCI resistance, and active-session protection must be supplied by a higher-level protocol.
A recorded M1 can be recomputed after compromise of the responder's static secret; the submission makes no forward-secrecy claim.
Key acceptance is below one, and the current numerical exponents are not certified upper bounds because the supplied double-precision computation truncates probabilities below 10^-13.
The 384/512 profiles use n=2048 and incur 2848-byte public keys, 3360-byte one-pass messages, and larger RAM costs.
Security rests on RLWE/split-RLWQ-Z hardness and transcript-bound SHAKE256 assumptions.
First-round performance covers reference C, x86-64 AVX2, and embedded-software portability; FPGA and ASIC performance are outside the claimed figures.
Performance measurements use one x86-64 AVX2 Linux/WSL environment; agreement tests report only 5,000 trials per profile and do not establish the tiny numerical rejection probabilities.

review_notes: M1 is treated as the only online transmitted message; pre-distributed pk_B is recorded separately and excluded from total_communication.
Table 4 sizes were cross-checked against all five params.h files and the NGCC KEX length-query implementation.
Initiator long-term API key objects are not treated as protocol requirements because the implementation states they exist only for harness compatibility.
conflicts: Section 7.1 contains stale MAMBA-NIKE-128 figures (1568-byte public key and 1824-byte message); authoritative Table 4, Table 9, params.h, and both self-evaluations agree on 1184 and 1568 bytes.
The specification title page spells Chengjing Tian, while the higher-priority basic-information form spells Chengjin Tian; the basic-information spelling is retained.

issues.description: No explicit mapping from the five named classical targets to NGCC level integers was found; stored as null rather than inferred.
Values are the submission's MATZOV-Q concrete estimator results, not separately stated target quantum-security levels.
The sampled contributor polynomial r is internal and not exposed as a canonical serialized key object, so its byte size is null.
Reported rejection exponents are explicitly not certified upper bounds; zero failures in 5,000 trials cannot validate those tail probabilities.
Chinese name forms were not present in the basic-information/specification text; stored as null.
